entries.finding: Party Room setup exposed a Seat Pass product choice instead of contextual Free or Paid room entry.
entries.repair: Replace the product-oriented control with Free/Paid Party Room entry, an exact price, a viewer preview, and a cancel-to-free lifecycle.

entries.finding: Live Stage entry and speaking-seat eligibility were not independently understandable or configurable.
entries.repair: Add independent Free/Paid viewer-entry and Free/Paid speaking-seat controls with exact public names and authority exclusions.

entries.finding: Ordinary creator and viewer surfaces used stale Ticket, Seat Pass, and Live Access wording.
entries.repair: Centralize and apply Party Room Pass, Live Stage Pass, Live Stage Seat Pass, and Event Pass display names without changing internal identities.

entries.finding: Paid Party Room copy did not unambiguously state exact room entry or exclude Live Stage and room/media authority.
entries.repair: Show the exact Party Room Pass, price, destination, authority exclusions, contextual CTA, and exact confirmation.

entries.finding: Paid Live Stage entry could be confused with a speaking-seat product.
entries.repair: Present Live Stage Pass as exact viewer/listener entry only, with a Watch Live CTA and no speaking or publish implication.

entries.finding: A paid-entry Live Stage lacked a client and database backstop requiring exact entry authority before a Seat Pass charge.
entries.repair: Enforce entry-first in the client and before pending seat purchase intents using the unchanged exact provider/grant authority.

entries.finding: Seat eligibility, a seat request, rejection, approval, current speaker membership, and removal were not durably distinguished.
entries.repair: Persist paid seat request/rejection state, derive approval from current canonical speaker membership, and render distinct host/viewer states without granting role authority.

entries.finding: A prior approved timestamp could continue to present approval after current speaker membership was removed or provider authority became stale.
entries.repair: Require exact active provider/grant proof for host state and current persisted speaker membership for Approved; refresh stale request state from server truth.

entries.finding: Seat purchase and request controls were reachable in hybrid mode but absent from the Live-first Stage mode.
entries.repair: Add the same exact Seat Pass explanation, purchase, and request controls to Live-first Stage overlay context.

entries.finding: Event access used generic paid-event wording and an allowed free or creator-preview state could masquerade as an active Event Pass.
entries.repair: Separate confirmed Event Pass, creator preview, and free Event states and retain exact Event-only routing with no inferred Live Stage authority.

entries.finding: Channel discovery could behave like a generic product catalog instead of letting the exact Party Room or Event choose its product.
entries.repair: Route discovery CTAs to the exact target where the contextual lock and purchase authority resolve.

entries.finding: Confirmations were generic or could remain stale while exact access became active.
entries.repair: Bind confirmation to exact offer/target readback and state the precise Party Room, Live entry, seat eligibility, or Event authority obtained.

entries.finding: Live purchase completion lacked bounded reconciliation polling and lifecycle refresh could leave duplicate or stale purchase CTAs.
entries.repair: Recognize already-purchased exact grants, poll exact provider reconciliation, and re-resolve access on foreground/resume.

entries.finding: Disabled Party Room, Live Stage, or Event offers could leave stale active display configuration.
entries.repair: Synchronize display-only config status from exact canonical offer status without deleting financial history.

entries.finding: Generic ticket/access notification labels did not communicate the exact product and destination.
entries.repair: Use public product names and exact Party Room, Live Stage seat context, and Event deep links for purchase, request, approval, rejection, refund, and reversal states.

entries.finding: Money Center exposed stale Party/Seat terminology and omitted clear Live Stage entry-versus-seat rows.
entries.repair: Render the four public names, exact target meaning, and separate Live Stage entry and seat summaries while retaining internal/provider identity behind the display layer.

entries.finding: Premium, Platform Subscription, VIP, Paid Video, Party Room, Live Stage, seat, and Event exclusions were inconsistently named.
entries.repair: Make cross-product exclusions explicit without changing #326 Premium, subscription, VIP, or Paid Video doctrine.

entries.finding: Long names, paired prices, and Live creator controls lacked complete wrapping, selected-state labels, and bounded scrolling/overlay behavior on small screens.
entries.repair: Add accessible labels/states, wrapping and minimum touch widths, a collapsible scrollable Live setup overlay, and exact CTA text.

entries.finding: The waiting-room join path checked Premium before resolving the exact Party Room offer, so an already-owned paid pass could be blocked even though hardened admission treats it as the exact paid-room authority; the direct route also misclassified a free-room response as a paid target.
entries.repair: Resolve exact Party Room offer/pass authority first, block a missing paid pass regardless of Premium, use exact paid authority when present, and retain the existing Premium prerequisite only for free Party Rooms.

entries.finding: Party Room resume could touch membership before an asynchronous pass refresh finished and could fail to restart bootstrap after a background purchase completed.
entries.repair: Revalidate exact Party Room Pass authority before membership touch, fail closed when a previously paid target cannot be verified, and restart bootstrap after pass recovery or background completion.

entries.finding: Client broadcast payloads could directly paint speaker, mute, or removal state before canonical persisted membership readback.
entries.repair: Treat seat-state broadcasts only as refresh hints and derive role, mute, removal, approval, and speaker presentation from persisted server state.

entries.finding: Purchase and terminal notifications could accept target metadata before resolving the exact Party Room or Live Stage offer, leaving a wrong-target route possible if metadata diverged from canonical offer state.
entries.repair: Resolve Party Room, Live Stage, and Event notification destinations from the exact creator/product-bound canonical offer or Event row and reject mismatched target metadata.

entries.finding: Generic creator setup could describe Live Stage products as App Store-backed on iOS even though #329 binds those exact sandbox products to Google Play, while iPhone viewer surfaces still rendered purchase CTAs that could only fail after a tap.
entries.repair: Keep both Live Stage product tiers bound to Google Play, disclose the Android-only sandbox reach in creator setup and confirmation copy, suppress unavailable viewer purchase controls on iPhone/non-Android builds, and make the internal diagnostic explain the same provider boundary without changing product identity.

entries.firstFailedBoundary: Party Waiting Room and Party Room checkout availability
entries.finding: The customer checkout shell treated live production-money activation as the authority for an otherwise valid closed-beta provider sandbox purchase, so an exact paid Party Room could be shown as unavailable while production money correctly remained off.
entries.repair: Use one bounded mobile/provider checkout-shell policy that admits either the existing production switch pair or closed-beta sandbox with live money, payouts and cashout all off; exact account, tester, intent, provider, product, buyer, creator, target, receipt and grant checks remain unchanged downstream.

entries.finding: A later authority wrapper replaced no-exact-offer free_room with seat_pass_not_available, and the Room UI then invented a $0.99 fallback, making a fresh free room appear paid. Owner status and underlying content monetization were not the cause.
entries.repair: Restore free_room only for one exact active title room with no current paid offer, retain authentication/current-session/restriction/host-block checks, delegate every paid or historical case to hardened authority, and remove invented price/currency fallbacks from both Party surfaces.

entries.finding: When the App Store reported an already-owned Premium subscription, the app polled backend authority without first running exact-account RevenueCat restore/reconciliation, then replaced the actionable result with generic inactive copy.
entries.repair: Recognize only the provider's exact already-owned signal, restore under the unchanged current account/session binding, poll authoritative backend Premium on a bounded state machine, preserve actionable delayed/different-account outcomes, and never treat provider state alone as entitlement authority.

entries.finding: The same recurring-subscription class lacked existing-purchase reconciliation and a visible exact-target Restore action.
entries.repair: Add current-account provider restore, exact creator subscription authority polling, bounded actionable states and an accessible Restore control without merging Platform Subscription with Premium or any room/Event pass.

entries.finding: Live Stage entry and seat purchases polled exact backend authority after a normal provider return but not after a non-cancellation provider/client race, allowing a completed exact grant to leave stale purchase UI.
entries.repair: Poll current-account, exact live target, exact offer and exact pass type after non-cancellation provider errors; confirm only server-backed entry or seat eligibility and preserve host approval and LiveKit publish separation.

entries.firstFailedBoundary: Waiting Room to Party Room display-context handoff
entries.finding: Final Android smoke first proved that the Party Room display lookup was coupled to the heavier playback-and-entitlement resolver. After that was separated, exact-main physical replay showed the remaining consumer defect: the Waiting Room resolved the exact public creator-video title but discarded it when routing, while Party Room launched a new display read as an unawaited, failure-swallowing side task and remained on Shared content despite the exact room/source row and public title being present.
entries.repair: Keep exact public display metadata separate from playback authority, carry the title resolved for the exact room source through a bounded in-process handoff keyed by exact party/source identity, and make Party Room bootstrap await its exact-target server refresh. User-controlled route parameters cannot supply the title fallback; cold/deep-link entry resolves from the exact server source. Playback, access, Premium, pass and media authority remain unchanged.
entries.proof: The focused executable RFGC contract requires the exact source-aware Waiting Room handoff, exact party/source matching at Party Room consumption, bounded expiry/entry count, and an awaited exact-target server refresh; it rejects a route title parameter, floating .then consumer, and playback, signed-source or entitlement work inside the display resolver. TypeScript, lint and affected media, route, LiveKit and monetization guards pass. Exact-main physical replay remains required after merge/OTA.

entries.finding: Final Android Party Room cleanup displayed Could not end room and the exact room remained active. entries.repair: Register request-save-replay explicitly as a self-authenticating Edge function, preserve exact signed-in host verification inside the function, require exact-room update readback instead of silently ignoring write failure, and redeploy only the exact merged function. The same repair closes Party Room and Live Stage end-without-saving and save-replay entry availability without weakening room, replay or LiveKit authority.
entries.proof: The replay policy guard and focused RFGC contract require explicit function deployment/auth config, in-function session and exact-host validation, exact-room end write readback, failure on missing targets, and both Party Room and Live Stage consumers. Exact deployed route and physical host end readback remain required after merge/deployment.

entries.finding: A read-only OPTIONS sweep of every active Edge Function found four registry-active routes returning NOT_FOUND_FUNCTION_BLOB: provider-readiness, spectator-start-room, request-save-replay, and creator-replay-playback. entries.repair: After exact source merge, redeploy only those four affected functions from protected main and read back each exact route/version/digest. No provider, room, replay, content, money, or LiveKit authority is moved to the client.
entries.proof: Existing provider-readiness, spectator child-room, replay request/playback and security guards remain the source contracts. Exact post-deployment route probes must return their contract-owned auth/input result rather than NOT_FOUND_FUNCTION_BLOB, and the physical Party Room host-end path must make the exact room inactive.

entries.proof: The focused RFGC and Premium sandbox Live proof execute the focus/resume, finite retry, stale-response rejection and original strict-gate recheck contracts; TypeScript, route, Android/iOS native, provider, notification and money guards pass.
